latest_release.name: macFUSE 5.5.0
latest_release.body:
### General

* Update the build process to use Xcode 27.1 (macOS 27.0 SDK)

* Build user-space components for `arm64e` in addition to `arm64` and `x86_64` to support Xcode's enhanced security build settings

### `FSModule` (`FSKit` Backend)

* Fix Disk Arbitration integration for volumes mounted with the `local` option so they appear as local volumes in Finder and can be unmounted through Finder

* Fix mounting on paths containing spaces and other non-ASCII characters. This addresses macfuse/macfuse#1198.

* Add support for read-only mounts on macOS 26.4 and later. This addresses macfuse/macfuse#1208.

* Add support for file preallocation through `FUSE_FALLOCATE`, using the same allocation flags as the kernel backend

* Fix extended attribute removal by sending `FUSE_REMOVEXATTR` instead of setting the attribute to an empty value. This addresses macfuse/macfuse#1213.

* Send `FUSE_FLUSH` when closing a file. This addresses macfuse/macfuse#1214.

  `FSKit` does not expose a per-file `fsync(2)` callback. On macOS 27, its close callback cannot return errors, so flush failures are logged but cannot be reported to the application through `close(2)`.

* Mitigate a data corruption issue in `FSKit` on macOS 26 and 27 by rejecting empty `FUSE_READ` replies with `EIO` and clearing unused buffer tails after short reads

  This workaround can cause read errors when a file's size changes remotely. This addresses macfuse/macfuse#1188.

* Add support for the `daemon_timeout` option and improve request cancellation by tracking `FUSE_INTERRUPT` requests, retrying interrupts after `EAGAIN`, and disconnecting unresponsive file system servers when interruption times out

* Improve item reclamation on macOS 27 by protecting items until FSKit has registered returned references, coordinating reclamation with concurrent lookups, and balancing lookup references and file handles on error paths

* Improve stability by validating incoming FUSE and XPC messages, checking buffer alignment, preventing request identifier collisions, and fixing races in request completion, cancellation, and timeout handling

* Improve concurrency and add fast paths for uncontended locks and semaphores

* Avoid repeated requests for access checks, flushes, preallocation, and file or directory synchronization when the file system server does not implement the corresponding callbacks

* Keep named pipes metadata-only and reject stream operations, size changes, and preallocation locally

* Fix a crash when mounting volumes using unsigned file system binaries on Intel Macs. This addresses macfuse/macfuse#1205.

### Kernel Extension (Kernel Backend)

* Update the kernel extension version to 5.5.0

* Add support for remote POSIX and BSD advisory locking, allowing file system servers to coordinate `fcntl(2)` and `flock(2)` locks across clients

  POSIX and BSD locking are negotiated independently. Local advisory locking remains available when neither capability is enabled. If only one family is enabled, requests for the other return `ENOTSUP`. Timed locks and PID-filtered lock queries are unsupported when remote locking is enabled.

  File system servers must track lock ownership using `fi->lock_owner` independently of `fi->fh`, because multiple lock owners can share a FUSE file handle. Close-time unlocks are sent explicitly instead of being inferred from flush or release requests.

* Add native I/O support for named pipes and character and block devices through macOS `fifofs` and `specfs`, while retaining FUSE namespace and metadata handling. This addresses macfuse/macfuse#1212

* Default kernel backend mounts to `nodev` to disable device access

  Mounting with `-o dev` requires root privileges. Named pipes are unaffected by `nodev`.

* Harden extended attribute reply handling by validating reply sizes before allocation and enforcing the advertised extended attribute size limit

detail.readme:
macFUSE
=======

macFUSE is a software package for macOS that lets non-privileged users create their own file systems without having to write a single line of kernel code. This is achieved by running file system code in user space while the macFUSE kernel extension provides only a "bridge" to the actual kernel interfaces.

About macFUSE
-------------

The latest version of macFUSE supports macOS 12 to macOS 27.

The software package provides multiple APIs for developing full-featured user space file systems. libfuse.dylib provides a superset of the standard Unix FUSE API. macFUSE.framework is a high-level Objective-C wrapper for the libfuse C API.

Developers can create numerous types of file systems using the provided APIs, e.g. on-disk file systems, layering file systems, network/distributed file system and many more. Three popular use cases are accessing files in the cloud, accessing files on non-native (unsupported by macOS) file systems and transparent encryption/decryption of files.

macFUSE file systems are regular applications (as opposed to kernel extensions). This means developers have as much flexibility and choice in programming tools, debuggers, and libraries as they have when developing regular application for macOS.

For more information see the [macFUSE website](https://macfuse.io), the official [macFUSE wiki](https://github.com/macfuse/macfuse/wiki) or the [community wiki](https://github.com/macfuse/community/wiki).

License
-------

Please see LICENSE.txt.

Source Code
-----------

This repository contains the source code of libfuse.dylib and macFUSE.framework. The other components, e.g. the macFUSE kernel extension, are closed-source.    

The source code of the last full open source release (version 3.8.3, supports macOS 10.5 to macOS 10.14.4), can be found in the [support/osxfuse-3](https://github.com/osxfuse/osxfuse/tree/support/osxfuse-3) branch on https://github.com/osxfuse/osxfuse/.
